items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: John Smith was a pimp. He had a lot of women dressed very good. He was in Ace Blossom, one of the Zulus Club. He was a band-girl.

ctx.x: But there's still, it's, uh, people like Dodds, and, uh, you know, Louis Armstrong, and so on, they, of course, they all went there, but...
Well, people engaged here more than us. People saw... stuff

I don't know anybody who would be the best friend, but you didn't get the opportunity to get off. That's when you were. Did you hear Johnny Dawes when you were married? I was Johnny Dawes. I was Johnny, I was Jimmy Newman, Charlie McQuirties, and he was one of the best. I was the man George Backing, he was one of the best. I was his brother. He was a kid, he was a kid. items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: I worked with uh, Wooden Joe, when Wooden Joe had a real old Wooden Joe's band with uh, with uh, Johnny Proudos, Buddy Luck, John Smith, uh, Edmund Garman, uh.

ctx.x: When you came back over here, you worked with Billy and the Dee some, didn't you?

Yeah, I worked with Billy and the Dee, I worked with uh, George, George Anderson, I worked with uh, Wooden Joe, when Wooden Joe had a real old Wooden Joe's band with uh, with uh, Johnny Proudos, Buddy Luck, John Smith, uh, Edmund Garman, uh.
